thread:
incident-bot: paging @maria_sre — ALB target failures reported in euc1-azc (multiple connection resets, rising 5xx). Automatic alert: 503 spike > 10% over 2m. Assess impact and coordinate.

maria_sre: Acked. I'm on it, looking at metrics and ALB health.

carlos_net: I'm seeing a ton of upstream reset logs from Envoy on the ingress nodes in az-c. Possible network flaps between ALB and nodeport targets.

ashley_eng: Copy — linking recent deploy? No deploys in last 30m from CI. Could be AZ-level networking.

maria_sre: Quick checks: curl from a healthy pod to local service returns 200. From ALB IPs we get ECONNRESET. Running aws CLI target health now.

carlos_net: Output from aws:
```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:...:tg/ingress-euc1-azc
TargetHealthDescriptions:
  - Id: ip-10-0-3-45
    State: unhealthy
    Reason: Target.ResponseCodeMismatch
  - Id: ip-10-0-3-46
    State: unhealthy
    Reason: Target.Timeout
```
Looks like multiple targets failing health checks.

maria_sre: Envoy logs snippet from ingress-2 (azc):
```
[warning] upstream reset: connection closed before response
[error] stream reset: 0x2
```

john_support: Customer impact: We're seeing support tickets from two customers in EU complaining about persistent 503s on dashboards and API. Oncall webhook also flagged a heap of failed background syncs.

maria_sre: Triage notes so far: ALB -> target IPs in az-c failing. Other AZs (aze, azb) show healthy targets. Immediate mitigation options: 1) remove az-c targets from ALB target group (quick), 2) shift traffic via Route53 failover/weighted routing (slower), 3) replace ALB with NLB pinned to healthy targets (disruptive).

carlos_net: Removing targets for az-c is fastest. I'll deregister the az-c targets from the target group to stop hitting them.

oncall-sre: Before you do that, set a short maintenance notice via status page and mark the group for quick rollback. Also let's record exact instance IPs.

carlos_net: Deregistering 3 targets in tg ingress-euc1-azc now.

incident-bot: action_log: carlos_net deregistered 3 targets from target-group arn:aws:... at 1805234622

maria_sre: Monitoring metrics... 503s dropped to baseline within 40s. Envoy reset errors reduced. Dashboard: 90th latency normalizing. Good sign.

ashley_eng: Suggest we cordon and drain the failing nodes in az-c to avoid re-registering bad targets after autoscaling. I'll create a script to drain pods off those nodes and trigger reboot/health-checks.

maria_sre: Agreed. Carlos, can you also open a ticket with cloud provider for possible AZ network degradation? Include packet loss/traceroutes.

carlos_net: Filing ticket now. Also running traceroute from healthy host to one of the failing target IPs — seeing intermittent hop timeouts at az-c internal router.

john_support: Notifying impacted customers with a brief 'partial outage in euc1' note and ETA 30m while we stabilize. I'll update as soon as we know more. :mega:

maria_sre: Per on-call runbook, we'll fail traffic to other AZs for 10m and monitor. If stable for 10m, we'll consider a rolling reboot of az-c hosts and re-register.

ashley_eng: Draining nodes in az-c now:
```
kubectl -n ingress cordon node/ip-10-0-3-45
kubectl -n ingress drain node/ip-10-0-3-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
Pods are rescheduling to azb/aze.

incident-bot: incident_status: mitigation_in_progress — targets deregistered, nodes cordoned/draining, cloud ticket opened.

carlos_net: Cloud provider replied: "We observe partial packet loss in AZ-C's internal fabric, investigating; recommend host reboot and avoid scheduling new targets until mitigation." They gave an internal ticket id: CPC-78991.

maria_sre: Plan: keep az-c targets out of rotation, finish draining, reboot hosts, wait for cloud provider fix, then run a small canary re-register (10% traffic) and observe for 15m before full restore. If canary fails, keep az-c out and escalate with provider.

john_support: I've updated customers with the mitigation plan and that we're routing around the failing AZ. Added a note to support triage to monitor escalations.

ashley_eng: After drains, envoy config is stable. No new reset logs. Repro curl against ALB endpoint yields 200 from multiple regions.

maria_sre: Status update (T+18m): 5xx rate back to normal, primary symptoms mitigated by removing az-c targets + draining. Customer impact reduced to intermittent errors while we moved traffic. I'll keep thread open for postmortem and handoff.

oncall-sre: Handoff to day SRE team in 20m for post-incident cleanup and follow-up (reboots, re-registering, and provider escalation). Leave thread pinned to incidents channel and tag me for final sign-off.

maria_sre: Copy. Creating a brief incident note for postmortem: cause suspected AZ internal network flap leading ALB target health failures -> Envoy connection resets -> 5xx spike. Immediate mitigation: target deregistration + drain + route traffic to healthy AZs. Next steps: provider follow-up, node reboots, canary re-register, update runbooks.

incident-bot: incident_closed_pending_postmortem: waiting for oncall sign-off. thread_ts: 1805234567

maria_sre: closing round: handing to day SRE @oncall-sre for postmortem and customer follow-ups. Please escalate if you see any regressions in the next 2 hours.

oncall-sre: Acknowledged. I'll pick this up and schedule the postmortem. Thanks everyone. :tada:
